backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/sync.rs:226 verify_hellosign_signature() MACs only `event_time + event_type` (`mac.update(format!("{}{}", event_time, event_type))`, L235) — the envelope_id is NOT part of the signed data.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/webhook.rs:848-861 the HELLOSIGN branch validates that tuple, then esignature_webhook acts on the UNSIGNED `payload.envelope_id` (L882-884) to resolve the owning org and mark that workflow completed/voided/declined (L906-967).

Consequence: an attacker who obtains ONE valid HelloSign notification (e.g. `signature_request_all_signed`) can replay it with an arbitrary substituted `envelope_id` in the JSON body — the event_hash still verifies (it only covers time+type) and the org is resolved FROM the attacker-chosen envelope_id, so an arbitrary, cross-tenant e-signature workflow is forged into a terminal signed/voided state. The DocuSign and Adobe branches are NOT affected: they verify_slice over the full raw `&body` (sync.rs:199/211), which binds envelope_id.

The idempotency guard in backend/crates/db/src/repositories/integration.rs:964-987 (`WHERE external_envelope_id = $1 AND status <> ALL($terminal)`) does NOT mitigate this: it only blocks re-transitioning an already-terminal workflow; a substituted, not-yet-terminal envelope_id passes the guard and is updated.

Fix: bind envelope_id into the authenticated set for HelloSign — either verify the full raw request body like the DocuSign/Adobe paths, or refuse to act on any payload field not covered by the provider signature; reject when the resolved workflow's provider != the verified provider.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/webhook.rs:747-972 esignature_webhook has NO timestamp/freshness (replay) check for ANY provider — grep for timestamp/freshness/tolerance/stale across the handler body returns nothing.

This is inconsistent with every sibling receiver in the same file, which all close the replay window per gap 83-3 / issue #2330: verify_portal_webhook (L1281-1323) and handle_portal_webhook fold a signed X-Webhook-Timestamp into the HMAC with a ±tolerance window; the Booking.com (L1110+) and Airbnb (verify_airbnb_delivery L1491) receivers do the same; reality-portal family documented in backend/CLAUDE.md.

For DocuSign/Adobe (full-body HMAC) a captured valid webhook can be replayed indefinitely to re-drive workflow state. For HelloSign, `event_time` IS signed but is never compared against server time (L848), so it provides no freshness. Combined with the envelope_id-binding gap above, replay is trivial.

Fix: reject deliveries whose provider-supplied timestamp is outside a tolerance window (HelloSign: validate `event_time`; DocuSign: `x-docusign-signature-1` carries a signed timestamp header set to verify; Adobe: enforce a received-at dedupe/nonce), matching the sibling receivers' pattern; persist a processed-delivery id for at-most-once handling.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/realtor-api.ts:22-49 — the shared `request<T>()` helper sends ONLY `credentials: 'include'` (cookie auth) and merges `{ 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...callerHeaders }`. It never calls `getAuthHeader()` from lib/auth-token.ts, and none of the exported callers (getMyRealtorProfile L67, updateMyRealtorProfile L71, createListing L117, getMyListing L129, updateListing L133, getMyRealtorAnalytics L148) pass an Authorization header. So no request from this module ever carries `Authorization Bearer <token>`.

This diverges from the sibling auth client lib/auth-api.ts:35-43, which deliberately merges BOTH `credentials: 'include'` AND `...getAuthHeader()` (comment L37-39: 'bearer header is additive — reality-server's extractor checks Authorization first then cookie'). lib/auth-token.ts is purpose-built for the email/password form-login path (docstring L1-11: persists the `/api/v1/users/login` JWT in localStorage under `ppt-portal-token` and adds `Authorization Bearer …` on authenticated requests) — that path sets NO `portal_session` cookie.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/extractors/auth.rs:31-44 — `extract_session_token` reads `Authorization Bearer …` first, then falls back to the `portal_session` cookie, returning None if neither is present. Consequence: a realtor authenticated via form-login (Bearer in localStorage, no cookie) sends neither mechanism on realtor write calls, so every createListing/updateListing/updateMyRealtorProfile/getMyListing/getMyRealtorAnalytics returns 401. The pages that call these directly (app/[locale]/realtor/listings/new/page.tsx:23, realtor/profile/page.tsx:68, realtor/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx, account/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx:129) surface a generic error and the realtor cannot create/edit listings or update their profile. Fix: merge `getAuthHeader()` into request()'s headers the same way auth-api.ts does. Confidence medium: correct if realtors can ever use form-login (the token module exists precisely for that); a no-op only if realtors are provisioned SSO-cookie-only in practice.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/states/ErrorState.tsx:59-66 hardcodes English default copy with no i18n: title='Something went wrong', description='Please try again. If the issue persists, contact support.', retryLabel='Try again'. components/states/EmptyState.tsx:16 defaults icon='📭' and takes plain-string title/description props with no translation.

Both are exported from the barrel components/states/index.ts:5-8 alongside StateView and LoadingSkeleton, but are currently UNRENDERED: grep for `<ErrorState`/`<EmptyState` finds only the unrelated LOCAL components defined inside components/import/CsvImport.tsx:1146 and FeedImport.tsx:906 (which ARE localized via useTranslations). The only barrel members actually imported anywhere are StateView (app/[locale]/error.tsx, not-found.tsx, agency/error.tsx, forbidden/page.tsx — all pass title={t(...)}) and LoadingSkeleton.

This is latent i18n debt, not a live user-facing bug: the shared ErrorState/EmptyState are the 'obvious' primitives a future dev will reach for, and unlike the already-safe StateView (which forces explicit title/description) they silently render English defaults. Low severity — fix is to either localize the defaults (accept a translation key / require callers to pass translated strings) or remove the dead exports so the localized StateView stays the single shared error/empty surface.
